provenance.what_this_is: DECLARED expectations for the synthetic mini corpus in ./mini_corpus. Every expectation below was written by a person from the fixture files' own contents, BEFORE any reader existed to produce them -- no parser output was consulted, harvested, or transcribed. A parser that scores itself is measuring nothing: it agrees with itself by construction and the report reads as a pass at any level of wrongness. `isaac_api.bl15.evaluate.load_gold_standard` refuses a document that declares otherwise, and `apps/api/tests/test_bl15_evaluate.py` asserts mechanically that no function in that module turns an `Observed` into a `GoldStandard`.
provenance.why_not_the_real_corpus: The real SSRL BL15-2 archive is real experimental data and real human notes and is never committed (CLAUDE.md 6). Its scientific ground truth is also not this repository's to declare -- the mapping questions are itemised in docs/bl15-2-domain-questions-2026-09-16.md and are Angel's. A gold standard for it would be this repository answering them. The STRUCTURAL counts for the real corpus are re-derivable instead, with scripts/bl15_corpus_report.py.
what_the_fixture_reproduces: 2.1 -- the extension does not classify: `runsynth` is extensionless and is a MACRO, `alignsynth` is extensionless and is a SPEC ACQUISITION
2.2 -- one macro is not one measurement: run01.mac declares two targets, Synth_XAS.mac declares none
2.3 -- a measurement can have ZERO scan children: the `_again` measurement has none
2.4 -- every `*_dir` also holds a byte-identical copy of its root acquisition file
2.5 -- macro intent vs acquired: `99_NEVER_ACQUIRED_SYN` is declared and never acquired
2.6 -- a duplicate legacy number: two distinct files carry `03`
2.6a -- internal `#F` disagreeing with the filename: the `ffilter35` file declares `beforeCycling` while its name says `after1500Cycling`
2.7 -- `ffilter35`, a doubled-prefix literal that must survive its own normalisation
3.5/3.7 -- one root readme.txt as beamtime-scope context, and a notes file whose broad claim contradicts its own sample section
the beamtime notes file begins with a UTF-8 BOM, exactly as the real one does
provenance.synthetic_marking: Every file carries a SYNTHETIC FIXTURE line, every sample name is SYN1/SYN2, every motor is prefixed `syn`, every energy is a round invented number and every timestamp is in 2099. Nothing here came from an instrument.

_comment_needs_domain_review_concepts: Concepts this gold standard DECLINES TO SCORE in the filename-token metric, because no literal expectation can be stated without asserting a scientific reading. `potential_reference_basis` because no source in this corpus family states one -- the official schema's `potential_scale` enum has six members and no 'unknown', so the honest act is absence, and that expectation is scored by its own dedicated metric rather than as a token. `loading_or_thickness` because `0p5nm` (an overlayer thickness) and `5wpc` (a weight loading) are two different physical quantities sharing one filename slot and the schema has a natural home for neither (mapping analysis 4); the fixture carries one so the deferral mechanism is exercised rather than merely described. This set governs SCORING, not extraction: a reader is still expected to READ and preserve both tokens, and `unknown_tokens` is where an unrecognised one must appear.
_comment_declared_normalization_rules: The rule names a `normalized` candidate may cite. The first two are `bl15.mapping`'s own rule names, quoted so the gold standard and the registry cannot drift apart; the third is the `ffilter35` rule, which the registry does not name because `filter` has no official path at all (mapping analysis 5) -- the normalisation is valid regardless of where the value lands. A candidate citing a rule that is not in this list is counted as fabricated, so a producer cannot legitimise an arbitrary transformation by inventing a name for it.
_comment_potential_reference_unresolved: ALL FOUR. No filename or header in this fixture states what the potential is measured against, and the official schema's own answer to that is vocabulary for absence (`rhe_basis: not_reported`), not a default. Leaving it absent is therefore RECOVERED here, and reporting a basis is a MISS -- the opposite polarity to every other metric in this file, and deliberate: a harness that scored an absent basis as a miss would improve as the reconstruction got less truthful.
_comment_filters: `ffilter35` is expected VERBATIM. The normalised reading (filter 35) belongs beside the literal with its rule named, never instead of it.
_comment_cycling_states: Read from the FILENAME. The `ffilter35` file's own `#F` header says `beforeCycling`, which is the conflict named below -- and the conflict is preserved rather than resolved, so neither reading overwrites the other and this expectation is about the filename only.
_comment_sample_groups: Grouped by the SECOND numeric token. Whether that token always means the sample/electrode instance is domain question 1 and is NOT settled here; this expectation is about the grouping a reader can perform from the name, not about what the group means.
_comment_measurement_groups: FIVE measurement units, FOUR of them with no scan children. An empty list is the RIGHT answer, not a gap: two of the real corpus's 94 units have zero scans, so 'every measurement has at least one scan' would be false of the real archive too.
_comment_macro_declarations: Three macro files, three declarations, and ZERO of them may become a Run. `runsynth` has no extension, so a macro inventory built from `*.mac` alone finds two of the three -- which is the same off-by-one the real corpus produces with `run29`.
_comment_readme_inheritance: One root readme.txt, no nested ones -- the same shape as the real archive, which is why nested-scope inheritance must not be designed against assumptions. Inherited context is BEAMTIME-scope evidence and must stay labelled as such; presenting it as a per-measurement entry would misstate where it came from.
_comment_duplicate_groups: By CONTENT digest, and every member is kept. Both copies are real files the scientist has; the only consequence of grouping is that they must not be counted as two independent witnesses to the same statement.
_comment_known_conflicts: FIVE named classes, mirroring the five the real corpus produces (characterization 2.5, 2.6, 2.6a, 2.7, 3.7). Scored BY NAME and never by count: a reconstruction that lost all five and invented five different ones would pass a count check perfectly. None of them may be silently resolved -- 'this is a conflict, not a defect to repair'.
_comment_unknown_tokens: An unrecognised token must be REPORTED, not dropped. Silently discarding the part of a filename a profile does not recognise leaves the scientist unable to see what was passed over, which is the banned Upload -> Spinner -> Mysterious JSON pattern one layer down.
_comment_technique: The fixture notes name HERFD and the official schema's `system.technique` enum contains `HERFD-XAS` verbatim, so this is a deterministic mapping rather than a judgement. `XAS` is also in the enum and is the weaker reading; an observation choosing it is recorded as a miss with both values named.
_comment_links: Both `rel` and `basis` values are in the official schema's enums verbatim. The `_again` token is the evidence for the first. The second rests on the second numeric token being the sample instance, which is domain question 1 -- it is declared here only because this fixture was AUTHORED with that meaning, which a real corpus cannot assert about itself.
